pumac-2010-power-01a.prompt:
A *graph* $G$ consists of a set $V(G)$ of vertices and a multiset $E(G)$ of *edges*, each an unordered pair $\{u,v\}$ of vertices (possibly $u=v$). Equal edges are *parallel*; an edge $\{v,v\}$ is a *loop*; a graph is *simple* if it has neither. Two vertices are *adjacent* if they form an edge. $K_n$ is the simple graph on $n$ vertices in which every two are adjacent; $K_{m,n}$ is the simple graph on $m+n$ vertices with $m$ vertices each adjacent to all $n$ others (and no other edges); $C_n$ has vertices $v_1,\dots,v_n$ and edges $\{v_i,v_{i+1}\}$ ($1\le i<n$) and $\{v_1,v_n\}$; the *wheel* $W_n$ is $C_n$ plus an extra vertex (the *hub*) adjacent to every vertex of $C_n$ by one edge.

**Problem 1.1 (2 points).** For which values of $n$ is $C_n$ simple?
